The public face, warm

Walked and drawn 2026-10-22 · round 1 ruled 2026-10-23 · runs beside Club Tier (owner, 2026-10-22)

What this page is for

A volunteer, coach or organizer should feel on day one that FieldLogicHQ was made to run their league or team, and not that they opened a terminal. This page walks the public face in the order a newcomer meets it, measures each stop on production, draws the end state for every surface, and asks you to rule. Nothing is built.

Round 1 ruled 2026-10-23

Twelve asks as recommended. Two differ: Ask 2 C, the wordmark is redrawn as its own piece of work before S4, and Ask 5 B, the marketing pages are always warm, whatever the visitor's setting. A follow-up the same day widened it: every signed-out page is warm, and signing out resets the browser to warm (Dark returns at sign-in).

The words in the frames are still drafts. /marketing settles them in each stage, before its code (Ask 4).

Ruled 2026-10-22: this runs beside Club Tier

Ahead of Platform admin. Only the order moved. The shape questions below are still recommendations.

The walk, the drawing and the marketing pages touch no club screen, so they can run any time. The email stage and the public bars carry coordination notes, set out on the ladder.

What the walk found

Today a newcomer passes through three different products.

1 · Old

The marketing site

It is always dark, whatever the visitor's setting. The typewriter face carries the navigation, the buttons and most of the running text, 120 to 190 times a page, and the stylesheet turns 40 to 70 of those into capitals. Four sections of the home page stay blank until you scroll.

2 · Warm

Sign-up, sign-in and the two account emails

The first look rebuilt these, and they reached production on 2026-10-20. The only typewriter text left is the wordmark. They no longer read as a terminal, so they are not reopened here.

3 · Old

Every other email and the error screens

About 44 emails still use the old dark card with lime capitals, and five more have their own copy of it. The 404 says "[DIAGNOSTIC]: ROUTE_NOT_FOUND" and offers to "Return to Root Node".

Push back first

The kickoff asked for disagreement before the work. These are argued from what the code and production do.

1 · Finding 1 is not too narrow. The first look's screens prove the fix.

Measured on production, the warm sign-in, forgot-password, Continue and step-one screens use the typewriter face for the wordmark and nothing else: 3 elements, none in capitals. They do not read as a terminal. So the marketing set needs the same treatment, written down as rules (S1) and applied as one set (S4), not a bigger redesign. Nothing in the drawings invents a new look.

The one widening: on the marketing pages the typewriter is not only in headings. Paragraphs, card text, checklists and plan details use it too (188 elements on Pricing). The plan's proposed build guard, "a public page that sets a heading in mono fails", would pass a page that still reads as a terminal. Ask 10 widens it.

2 · Q1 reverses a ruling. Here is what that ruling protected.

The 2026-07-23 entry ("Marketing pages … stay dark by design") gives one reason: "M2 unchanged". M2 is the rule that an organization's own brand wins on its own pages. Our marketing pages carry no organization's brand, so that reason never applied to them. What the dark ruling did protect, through S1-2 (2026-07-20), is that the marketing set moves as one. The end state keeps that: the bar, the footer and all 13 marketing routes change in one release (S4), never one page at a time.

3 · Q6 belongs in its own project, not a stage here.

The public tournament pages are 35 routes and the heaviest typewriter users in the product (the schedule alone has 38 uses). Two standing rulings sit on them: R1-2 (walking into an event is "walking into the venue") and R1-4 (the typewriter stays for scores and records). The new club site already uses Barlow and Inter, so what is left is the tournament pages, and families read them more than anyone. They need their own walk and drawing, and they overlap Tinted Panel Retirement's "second wave" (D4), which already owns their panels.

The cost of each choice: as a stage here, this project roughly doubles and its walk becomes a families walk. As its own project, tournament pages keep the typewriter capitals for one project longer. Recommended: its own project, joined with D4, drawn after S4 so it inherits the S1 rules. Ask 7.

4 · Half the email stage should not wait for Club.

Moving the shared email shell onto the warm envelope (S3a) changes no email's words. The Club stages that add emails have not started: Stage 9 (house league, whose seven league emails are on the old shell) and Stage 12 (the payment receipt "in the club's name"). If the shell moves first, those stages are built warm and nobody restyles them afterwards. If it waits, both stages write onto the dark shell and S3 does them again.

The half that should wait: the family emails in the club's own name (S3b, Q5). That is 7c's sender, its open follow-up (moving the house-league season email onto the batched sender), and the same question Stage 12's receipt asks. Ask 9.

5 · Two coordination notes in the plan were wrong

  • The plan says marketing pages are demo tour destinations. They are not. The build guard checks product screens and the "See it live" door only. Restyling the marketing pages cannot break a tour. The plan is corrected.
  • Stage 13 covers the operator navs only (sidebar, phone bar, More sheet, top strip). The public bars are not in its inventory. So their lettering belongs to this project, as P1 (2026-10-19) handed it here. Only the crossing, a signed-in visitor's "Open app" door from the marketing bar into a portal, is marked "coordinate with Stage 13". Nothing here draws a navigation answer.

6 · Found outside the look, routed rather than fixed here

  • To /marketing: the home page's description (what a search result shows) says "for Canadian sports organizations", which breaks the brand rule "never claim Canadian identity". PRICING_PAGE_COPY.md has the same line. The Pricing tab title reads "Pricing — FieldLogicHQ | FieldLogicHQ". The house-league card on the home page says parents get "automated game notifications without staff sending a single email". Club Tier's Stage 9 defect list says league communications "silently email nobody", so that line may break the 2026-10-19 truth rule. Found by the flow check: the Premium welcome email says "Everything from your free portal carries over", though most new Premium coaches never had a free portal. Marketing emails sign off "FieldLogicHQ · Canada", which breaks the brand rule and is a thin mailing address for CASL.
  • To /strategy (finding 6): there is no privacy policy or terms page, and nothing links to one. That is a trust and compliance question for a product that takes sign-ups and family data, not a look question. It is recorded as its own item.

How to read the drawings

Every tag, flag and fix chip opens its explanation when tapped. Captures are from production (www.fieldlogichq.ca) on 2026-10-22, signed out. The emails are rendered from the code's built-in defaults: nothing was sent, and the database was not read (an operator can customise a template). Desktop drawings are 1440 wide and fit to the window. "Show at true size" shows them at full size. Phone drawings are 390 wide, at true size, scrolling inside an 844-high frame.

The measured walk

Fourteen stations, in the order a newcomer meets them. Each one shows as built (production captures and measured type), my read, and the shape question it raises, with a notes box. Your notes travel with the asks' paste-back.

Desktop, production. The first screen.

The full length at half size. The two blank bands are four sections waiting for a scroll before they appear.

Phone. The five role links sit in a bottom strip in typewriter capitals.

Measured

Ground #0A0A0A always. A Dark or light device setting changes nothing.
Headline "Less admin. More sport.": Barlow Condensed 900, 88px.
Section headings: Barlow 800, 38–44px.
Nav links: IBM Plex Mono 12.5px 600, CAPITALS.

Typewriter face on 189 elements, 69 in capitals.

My read

  • Works: the headline and its promise are right, and the hero paragraph is already Inter. The Founding Season offer is clear.
  • Gets in the way: after the headline, everything is a console: capitals in the bar, typewriter paragraphs in the cards, a grid behind the page and square buttons.
  • I'd change: paper ground, Barlow 700 headings in sentence case, Inter for every sentence, sentence-case navigation and buttons, and nothing hidden until scrolled. The words stay unless /marketing changes them.
ReshapeQ1 · Supersede "marketing stays dark", moving the whole set together

Recommended. The drawings move the bar, the footer and every marketing page in one release. Ask 1 · Dark visitors: Ask 5

What rides on it: 13 marketing routes, the marketing bar and footer, and one shared stylesheet each for the walkthroughs and the plan cards. Restyling them cannot break a demo tour.

11The 404, crash, offline, unsubscribe and paused screens Old

The 404. Warm colours, terminal words.

Offline. Already plain and warm.

Unsubscribed. A dark card on near-black.

Measured, words verbatim

404: "Diagnostic Output" · "404" · "[DIAGNOSTIC]: ROUTE_NOT_FOUND" · "Requested resource is outside the current system scope. Verify the URL and retry, or return to root." · "Return to Root Node" (mono caps, spaced). Every line is typewriter.
Crash: "System Diagnostic Report" · "[SYSTEM]: INTERNAL_FAULT" · "An unhandled exception was encountered during request processing." · "Retry Request" · "Return to Root".
Fatal crash (before styles load): dark, hard-coded monospace, "[SYSTEM]: FATAL_FAULT".
Offline: system sans, sentence case, "You're offline" · "Try again". Only its little "FIELDLOGICHQ" mark is in capitals.
Unsubscribed: dark #0b0f14 card, Inter, sentence case; mono caps wordmark spaced .18em.
Paused workspace: the last screen on the old sign-in stylesheet (mono caps title and button), "Workspace access paused". Not captured, because it needs a suspended account.

My read

  • Gets in the way: a lost volunteer is told they asked for a resource "outside the current system scope". That is the clearest terminal moment in the product.
  • I'd change: plain sentences that say what happened and the way forward, in the sign-in screens' type. Offline needs only its mark.
ReshapeS5 · system screens

Standing back: the public type rules

These cut across every station. They are the first look's written rules (its plan, rules 1–8), extended from the sign-up screens to the marketing site, the emails and the system screens. S1 writes them down once, with /design and /marketing, as part of the identity.

RuleWhat it saysWhere today breaks it
P1 · The typewriter face is for the wordmark, a plan chip and real dataNever a sentence, a label, a button, a heading or a navigation link. (Scores and records on the sport pages are data, so R1-4 keeps them. That belongs to Q6's project.)Marketing: 66–1,002 elements a page, including paragraphs and plan lists. The 404 and crash. The chooser's labels.
P2 · One heading faceBarlow Condensed 700, sentence case. A page has one face for its headings.Barlow 900, Barlow 800, and IBM Plex Mono 700 at 52 and 60px. The For pages mix two faces.
P3 · Sentence case wherever a person readsThe only capitals are the eyebrow line (Inter 600 12, letter-spaced, olive: the first look's step line, coloured) and a plan chip.40–70 elements a page in capitals by stylesheet, 519 on the changelog.
P4 · A button says what happensInter 700, sentence case, 48px, lime fill with ink text, 10px corners, no arrow. One lime button per view. Secondary: white with an edge. A text link is olive."START FREE — NO CREDIT CARD REQUIRED", "Accept invite →", "Return to Root Node".
P5 · Paper by default, Dark by choice, no dark islandThe public face follows the visitor's Warm / Dark choice and is warm without one. Lime is a fill, never text on paper (E3).The marketing set and the unsubscribe page are always dark.
P6 · Complete when it loadsNothing waits for a scroll to appear. A screenshot, a slow phone and a skimming reader see the whole page.Four home sections.
P7 · Every page says what it is when sharedA title, a description and a share card.The marketing site has none.
P8 · No system wordsSay what happened and the way forward, in one sentence each.The 404, the crash and the fatal crash.
P9 · One wordmarkFIELD ink · LOGIC olive · HQ dim, IBM Plex Mono 700 (Courier New in email, which cannot load our fonts). On dark: FIELD white · LOGIC lime · HQ dim.Five versions today: the marketing bar, the consumer bar, the footer, the emails (lime capitals spaced .16em), and the unsubscribe page (spaced .18em).
P10 · One email envelopeThe warm envelope the first look built. A family email adds the club's identity to it (Q5) and never replaces it.About 44 emails on the old shell and 5 with their own copies.

The type ladder stays the portal's (--type-*: 32 · 24 · 20 · 16 · 14 · 12 · 11 · 10). The one thing a marketing page needs that the ladder lacks is a poster-size headline, one per page. Ask 3 asks whether that is a named exception, the way the first look's Ask 12 made one.

The identity, written once (S1)

The brand docs cover positioning ("community sport"), voice ("Practical. Direct. Warm.") and audience. They never cover type, colour or the wordmark (finding 5). This is the proposal, built from what the portal and the first look already ship, so it adds nothing new to learn. Q2's starting point was to keep the typewriter lockup and the ">" mark and soften everything around them. The first look has already shipped half of that: the consumer bar and the account emails wear the three-ink wordmark.

Voice

"Practical. Direct. Warm. Like the most organized person on the volunteer board." The rule for this project: write from the volunteer's side of the screen, name what happens next, and use no system words. Every changed line is a draft until /marketing settles it.

The end state, drawn

One proposal per surface, at true size, a desktop and a phone for each. Every changed part carries its tag and the stage that delivers it. Nothing here is an intermediate state: this is what the public face looks like when S1–S5 are done. Words are today's unless tagged DRAFT WORDS.

The click into sign-up

S4 · Ask 13

"Get started" and "Start free" both land on the chooser, inside the consumer bar the first look ruled. After S4 the two bars share the wordmark, the lettering and the button, but they stay two bars with different links: the marketing bar lists the roles, and the consumer bar lists Home and Scores. One thing breaks the way back. On the sign-up screens the wordmark leads to the fan app's home (Discover), not to the page the newcomer came from (Ask 13). On a phone, an install banner also sits over every sign-up step today; S5 keeps it off them.

Home, for a visitor who chose Dark

Not taken · Ask 5 ruled always warm

The setting is this browser's last Warm / Dark choice, so a Dark user on a new phone sees warm until they choose again. If Ask 5 is ruled "follow the setting", a signed-out visitor gets warm, and someone who chose Dark keeps it after signing out. This is the portal's Dark, the same as sign-in's, not today's marketing dark. Lime may be text here, because E3 applies to paper only.

Every email on one envelope

S3a

The envelope is the one the first look built (station 5), drawn faithfully: white card, three-ink wordmark, Arial, a lime button with an olive edge. These emails only move onto it. Their words come along, minus capitals and arrows. A desktop mail pane is 640 wide; a phone is 390.

What arrives, in order, for each door (today's sends, from the code)

DoorFirstThen
Start a team (free)Confirm your email (warm)Nothing else. The verify link works for 1 hour.
Run a tournament (free)Confirm your email (warm)A Tournament Plus suggestion about a week later (old dark, S3a)
Run a tournament on Tournament PlusConfirm your email (warm)"You're on Tournament Plus" about a day later (old dark, S3a)
Coach a team (Premium)Confirm your email (warm)The Premium welcome, minutes later, once the team is set up (old dark, S3a; drawn below)

Until S3a ships, every door except the free team gets a warm email and then a dark one. That is why the ladder puts S3a ahead of S4. Whether a free team should get a "here is your team" email is a new email, so it goes to /marketing and /strategy.

S3b · Ask 6

The same warm envelope, with the club's identity added: a band in the club's colour, its logo and name where our wordmark sits, and the button in the club's colour when white text on it passes contrast (ink on lime when it does not). FieldLogicHQ moves to the footer. Riverdale's navy is a stand-in for any club's colour.

Both checks ran on round 1 of this page (2026-10-22), before the hand-off. Every change marked "Drawn" is already in the drawings you are looking at. Everything here is a proposal until you rule: Ask 12 accepts or trims the drawn changes, and Ask 13 and Ask 14 carry the two calls that need you.

Asks

Round 1 ruled 2026-10-23

Twelve asks as recommended. Two differ: Ask 2 C, the wordmark is redrawn as its own piece of work before S4, and Ask 5 B, the marketing pages are always warm, whatever the visitor's setting.

The words in the frames are still drafts. /marketing settles them in each stage, before its code (Ask 4).

One pick per ask. The recommended option is marked. Your picks, your notes and your station notes stay in this browser. Copy all answers at the foot gives one block to paste back. Q8 (the order) is ruled: this runs beside Club Tier. Q1–Q7 are below, plus seven the walk and the checks raised.

Ask 1Marketing stays dark (2026-07-23): supersede it? (Q1)

That ruling's only written reason was "M2 unchanged", and M2 is about an org's own pages. What it protected in practice is that the marketing set moves together.

What rides on it: the whole of S4, and the design log entry that records the reversal (with its reason, not its date).

Ask 2The wordmark and the mark (Q2)

What rides on it: the marketing bar, the consumer bar, the footer, the unsubscribe page and the email envelope all draw one wordmark. B adds the mark to two bars. C pauses S4 behind a brand project.

Ask 3The public type rules (S1), and the marketing headline's size

The rules are on the Rules tab (P1–P10): the first look's rules, extended to marketing, emails and system screens. The one gap is a poster headline. The ladder tops out at 32px, and a marketing hero at 32px reads as a form heading.

What rides on it: every S4 drawing's headline, and what the build guard (Ask 10) checks.

Ask 4The words (Q3)

What rides on it: help articles that quote screen wording (/docs runs on each stage) and the spelling and clock gates.

Ask 5Warm / Dark on the marketing pages (Q4)

What rides on it: A doubles S4's checking (each page in both looks), and the marketing set reads the same setting as the rest of the product.

Ask 6Family emails: whose look? (Q5)

What rides on it: the family email, the dues reminder, the club schedule emails and the basic coach announcement. A reads each club's logo and colour, so a club without a custom logo falls back to the colour-made one.

Ask 7The public tournament pages' type (Q6)

What rides on it: 35 routes, and whether this project's last stage is family-facing.

Ask 8Link previews (Q7)

What rides on it: B touches every tournament's share card, which belongs with Ask 7's project if that is ruled separate.

Ask 9When the email stage runs, given Club

What rides on it: B means Stages 9 and 12 build on the dark shell and S3 restyles them afterwards. C may collide with 7c's sender follow-up.

Ask 10A build guard for the public type

What rides on it: a new check beside the spelling and clock gates, built in S1 and switched on per stage as each surface is restyled.

Ask 11The ladder's order

What rides on it: the first build prompt is written for the first stage after S1.

Ask 12The design and flow checks' drawn changes

Listed on the Checks tab: D1–D4 and D7–D12, U2–U4, U6 and U8, all already in the drawings. D5, D6 and U1 are Asks 13 and 14.

Ask 13Where the wordmark leads during sign-up

On the sign-up screens a signed-out newcomer's only way back to the page they came from is the browser's Back button. The wordmark leads to the fan app's home (Discover).

What rides on it: one link on the bar the first look ruled. Its look is untouched. It is not a crossing between portals, so it is not Stage 13's.

Ask 14One lime button per view on the marketing pages

P4 says one lime per view. Today the bar's lime "Get started" sits above each page's own lime, Pricing shows four, and the home page's first screen has no button of its own.

What rides on it: which plan Pricing nudges toward, a commercial choice as much as a design one. If it matters to you, /strategy can record it. C would also mean re-ruling Demos and the plan step, which draw one lime.
